cases.sentence: ___ ужасно разозлился; ему вдруг захотелось как-нибудь оскорбить этого жирного франта.
options: Раскольников
Раскольникова
Раскольникову
Раскольниковым
cases.translation: Raskolnikov became terribly angry; he suddenly wanted to insult this fat dandy somehow.
cases.explain: "Раскольников" is the subject of the verb "разозлился" (became angry), so the surname stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: …в стороне, шагах в пятнадцати, на краю ___, остановился один господин…
options: бульвар
бульвара
бульвару
бульваром
cases.translation: …off to one side, some fifteen paces away, at the edge of the boulevard, a gentleman had stopped…
cases.explain: The phrase "на краю" (at the edge of) governs the genitive case, giving "бульвара."

cases.sentence: Он на минуту оставил девочку и подошел к ___.
options: господин
господина
господину
господином
cases.translation: He left the girl for a moment and walked over to the gentleman.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (toward) always governs the dative case, giving "господину."

cases.sentence: И, схватив ___ за руку, он потащил его к скамейке.
options: городовой
городового
городовому
городовым
cases.translation: And, seizing the policeman by the arm, he dragged him toward the bench.
cases.explain: The verb "схватив" (having grabbed) takes a direct object in the accusative case; for this animate masculine noun the accusative form matches the genitive: "городового."

cases.sentence: Раскольников бросился на него с ___, не рассчитав даже и того, что плотный господин мог управиться и с двумя такими, как он.
options: кулаки
кулаков
кулакам
кулаками
cases.translation: Raskolnikov threw himself at him with his fists, without even calculating that the stout gentleman could have handled two men like him.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) governs the instrumental case, giving the plural form "кулаками."

cases.sentence: Или отказаться от жизни совсем! — вскричал он вдруг в ___, — послушно принять судьбу, как она есть.
options: исступление
исступления
исступлению
исступлении
cases.translation: Or give up life entirely! he suddenly cried out in a frenzy — submissively accept fate as it is.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" describing a state governs the prepositional case, giving "исступлении."

reading.ru: Не бывать этому браку, пока я жив, и к черту господина Лужина!
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov decide immediately regarding Dunya's planned marriage?
options: That the marriage will not happen while he is alive, and to hell with Luzhin
That he fully approves of the match
That he needs more time to think it over
That he will write to Luzhin to thank him
reading.correct: That the marriage will not happen while he is alive, and to hell with Luzhin
reading.explain: He decides at once and finally that this marriage shall never take place while he lives, cursing Mr. Luzhin.

reading.ru: И эта же Дунечка за это же кажется замуж идет!..
reading.question: What bitter observation does Raskolnikov make about Dunya's reason for marrying Luzhin?
options: That she is marrying him for the mere impression that he "seems" kind
That she is marrying him purely for love
That she is marrying him against her own will entirely
That she refuses to marry him at all
reading.correct: That she is marrying him for the mere impression that he "seems" kind
reading.explain: He mocks that Dunya is marrying Luzhin based merely on the fact that he "seems" kind, repeating the word with bitter irony.

reading.ru: Злоба накипала в нем всё сильнее и сильнее, и если бы теперь встретился с ним господин Лужин, он, кажется, убил бы его!
reading.question: How intense does Raskolnikov's anger toward Luzhin become?
options: So intense that he feels he could kill Luzhin if they met right then
Mild annoyance that quickly fades
He feels nothing but indifference toward Luzhin
He feels sympathy for Luzhin's situation
reading.correct: So intense that he feels he could kill Luzhin if they met right then
reading.explain: The narrator says his anger boiled ever stronger, and that had Luzhin appeared at that moment, he seemed ready to kill him.

reading.ru: Главное, „человек деловой и, кажется, добрый“: шутка ли, поклажу взял на себя, большой сундук на свой счет доставляет!
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov sarcastically cite as proof of Luzhin's supposed kindness?
options: That he took charge of the luggage and pays to deliver a large trunk himself
That he wrote Dunya a love poem
That he gave the family a large sum of cash
That he offered to cancel the wedding
reading.correct: That he took charge of the luggage and pays to deliver a large trunk himself
reading.explain: Raskolnikov sarcastically notes that, as proof of Luzhin's business-like kindness, he took the luggage upon himself and delivers a large trunk at his own expense.

reading.ru: Нет, Дуня не та была, сколько я знал, и… ну да уж, конечно, не изменилась и теперь!..
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov conclude about whether Dunya's character has changed?
options: That she was not the type to compromise before, and surely has not changed now
That she has become much weaker and more submissive
That he no longer knows her at all
That she has become exactly like their mother
reading.correct: That she was not the type to compromise before, and surely has not changed now
reading.explain: He reflects that Dunya was never one to yield her principles, and is certain she has not changed even now.

reading.ru: А ты что теперь делаешь? Обираешь их же.
reading.question: What accusation does Raskolnikov level against himself regarding his family's money?
options: That he is plundering/fleecing them himself by taking their scarce money
That he has given all his money away to strangers
That he refuses to accept any help from them
That he has found a job to support them
reading.correct: That he is plundering/fleecing them himself by taking their scarce money
reading.explain: He turns the accusation on himself, admitting that right now he is the one fleecing them of their money.

reading.ru: Или отказаться от жизни совсем! — вскричал он вдруг в исступлении, — послушно принять судьбу, как она есть, раз навсегда, и задушить в себе всё, отказавшись от всякого права действовать, жить и любить!
reading.question: What extreme alternative does Raskolnikov cry out about in his frenzy?
options: Giving up life entirely and submissively accepting fate, renouncing every right to act, live, and love
Running away to another country immediately
Confessing everything to the police at once
Marrying quickly to solve his financial troubles
reading.correct: Giving up life entirely and submissively accepting fate, renouncing every right to act, live, and love
reading.explain: In a frenzy he cries out that the alternative is to give up life altogether, submissively accept fate, and stifle every right to act, live, and love.

reading.ru: Ему стукнуло в голову, и потемнело в глазах.
reading.question: What physical reaction does Raskolnikov have when the terrible thought returns to him in a new, threatening form?
options: A pounding sensation in his head and darkness before his eyes
A sudden burst of energy and clarity
Uncontrollable laughter
A feeling of complete calm
reading.correct: A pounding sensation in his head and darkness before his eyes
reading.explain: The text describes a pounding sensation striking his head and his vision going dark as the idea returns in a menacing new form.

reading.ru: Он поспешно огляделся, он искал чего-то.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do as his agitation grows on the boulevard?
options: He hurriedly looks around, searching for something (a bench to sit on)
He runs straight home
He calls out for help
He sits down calmly and reads a book
reading.correct: He hurriedly looks around, searching for something (a bench to sit on)
reading.explain: He hastily looks around, searching for something — he wants to sit down and is looking for a bench.

reading.ru: Пред ним было чрезвычайно молоденькое личико, лет шестнадцати, даже, может быть, только пятнадцати, — маленькое, белокуренькое, хорошенькое, но всё разгоревшееся и как будто припухшее.
reading.question: How is the drunken young girl on the bench described?
options: A very young face, about fifteen or sixteen, small, blonde, pretty, but flushed and swollen-looking
An elderly woman with gray hair
A tall, athletic young man
A well-dressed, sober lady of high society
reading.correct: A very young face, about fifteen or sixteen, small, blonde, pretty, but flushed and swollen-looking
reading.explain: The narrator describes her extremely young face, about fifteen or sixteen, small, fair-haired, pretty, but flushed and somewhat swollen.

reading.ru: Раскольников ужасно разозлился; ему вдруг захотелось как-нибудь оскорбить этого жирного франта.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov suddenly want to do to the well-dressed gentleman watching the girl?
options: Insult the fat dandy somehow
Introduce himself politely
Ask him for money
Warn him about the police
reading.correct: Insult the fat dandy somehow
reading.explain: Raskolnikov becomes furious and suddenly wants to insult this fat dandy in some way.

reading.ru: Вам чего тут надо? — крикнул он, сжимая кулаки и смеясь своими запенившимися от злобы губами.
reading.question: What odd name does Raskolnikov shout at the strange gentleman?
options: Svidrigailov
Luzhin
Marmeladov
Razumikhin
reading.correct: Svidrigailov
reading.explain: Raskolnikov shouts "Hey you, Svidrigailov!" at the stranger, clenching his fists — foreshadowing the character who will later appear under that real name.

reading.ru: Раскольников бросился на него с кулаками, не рассчитав даже и того, что плотный господин мог управиться и с двумя такими, как он.
reading.question: What reckless action does Raskolnikov take against the gentleman?
options: He throws himself at him with his fists, without considering the man's strength
He calmly asks him to leave
He calls a policeman first
He simply walks away
reading.correct: He throws himself at him with his fists, without considering the man's strength
reading.explain: Raskolnikov attacks with his fists without calculating that the stout gentleman could easily have handled two men like him.

reading.ru: Это было бравое солдатское лицо с седыми усами и бакенами и с толковым взглядом.
reading.question: How is the policeman who intervenes described?
options: A fine soldierly face with gray mustache and side-whiskers and an intelligent gaze
A young, inexperienced recruit
An angry, red-faced brute
A frail old man barely able to stand
reading.correct: A fine soldierly face with gray mustache and side-whiskers and an intelligent gaze
reading.explain: The narrator describes the policeman as having a fine, soldierly face with gray mustache and whiskers and a sensible look.

reading.ru: Вернее же всего где-нибудь напоили и обманули… в первый раз… понимаете? да так и пустили на улицу.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov suspect really happened to the drunken girl?
options: That she was plied with drink and deceived somewhere, for the first time, then simply turned loose on the street
That she ran away from a wealthy family on purpose
That she is a professional performer resting between shows
That she is simply exhausted from walking too far
reading.correct: That she was plied with drink and deceived somewhere, for the first time, then simply turned loose on the street
reading.explain: Raskolnikov explains to the policeman that most likely she was made drunk and deceived somewhere for the first time, then simply put out onto the street.

reading.ru: Ах, жаль-то как! — сказал он, качая головой, — совсем еще как ребенок.
reading.question: How does the policeman react upon looking closely at the girl?
options: With genuine pity, remarking she is still just like a child
With harsh scorn and disgust
With complete indifference
By laughing at her appearance
reading.correct: With genuine pity, remarking she is still just like a child
reading.explain: The policeman shakes his head, expressing pity and noting that she is still quite like a child.

reading.ru: Девушка открыла усталые и посоловелые глаза, тупо посмотрела на допрашивающих и отмахнулась рукой.
reading.question: How does the girl respond when the policeman asks where she lives?
options: She opens her weary, glazed eyes, stares blankly, and waves them off with her hand
She gives her exact address clearly
She bursts into tears and explains everything
She stands up and runs away immediately
reading.correct: She opens her weary, glazed eyes, stares blankly, and waves them off with her hand
reading.explain: The girl opens her tired, glazed eyes, looks dully at her questioners, and waves her hand dismissively.

reading.ru: Ах, стыд-то какой теперь завелся на свете, господи! Этакая немудреная, и уж пьяная!
reading.question: What does the policeman lament about the state of the world, seeing the drunk young girl?
options: That such shameful things now happen — even so simple a girl already drunk
That the police no longer have any power
That drink has become too expensive for common people
That young girls no longer respect their elders
reading.correct: That such shameful things now happen — even so simple a girl already drunk
reading.explain: The policeman laments the shame of the modern world, remarking on how such a simple girl is already drunk.

reading.ru: Та вдруг совсем открыла глаза, посмотрела внимательно, как будто поняла что-то такое, встала со скамейки и пошла обратно в ту сторону, откуда пришла.
reading.question: What does the girl finally do after seeming to understand something?
options: She opens her eyes fully, gets up from the bench, and walks back the way she came
She falls asleep again on the bench
She thanks Raskolnikov and the policeman warmly
She asks to be taken to a hospital
reading.correct: She opens her eyes fully, gets up from the bench, and walks back the way she came
reading.explain: She suddenly opens her eyes fully, looks attentively as if understanding something, rises from the bench, and walks back the way she had come.

reading.ru: В эту минуту как будто что-то ужалило Раскольникова; в один миг его как будто перевернуло.
reading.question: What sudden change comes over Raskolnikov as the policeman starts to follow the girl and the dandy?
options: Something seems to sting him, and he is instantly transformed inside
He feels a sudden wave of relief
He falls asleep standing up
He decides to follow them himself
reading.correct: Something seems to sting him, and he is instantly transformed inside
reading.explain: At this moment something seems to sting Raskolnikov, and in an instant he is completely turned around in his feelings.

reading.ru: Оставьте! Чего вам? Бросьте! Пусть его позабавится (он указал на франта).
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov suddenly tell the policeman to do, reversing his earlier concern for the girl?
options: To leave it alone and let the dandy "amuse himself" with her
To arrest the dandy immediately
To take the girl to the hospital himself
To give her more money
reading.correct: To leave it alone and let the dandy "amuse himself" with her
reading.explain: Raskolnikov abruptly tells the policeman to leave it, to drop it, and let the dandy amuse himself, pointing at him.

reading.ru: Двадцать копеек мои унес, — злобно проговорил Раскольников, оставшись один.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov bitterly remark to himself once left alone?
options: That the policeman carried off his twenty kopecks
That he has lost his hat again
That he should have stayed to help more
That the girl stole money from him
reading.correct: That the policeman carried off his twenty kopecks
reading.explain: Left alone, he says spitefully that his twenty kopecks were carried off (by the policeman).

reading.ru: Бедная девочка!.. — сказал он, посмотрев в опустевший угол скамьи.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov say, looking at the now-empty corner of the bench?
options: "Poor girl!.."
"Good riddance!"
"She deserved it"
"I must follow her"
reading.correct: "Poor girl!.."
reading.explain: Looking at the emptied corner of the bench, he says, "Poor girl!..", imagining her likely tragic future.

reading.ru: На Васильевский остров, к Разумихину я пошел, вот куда, теперь… помню.
reading.question: Where does Raskolnikov realize he was originally headed?
options: To Vasilyevsky Island, to see Razumikhin
To the pawnbroker's apartment
To the police station
To his mother's house
reading.correct: To Vasilyevsky Island, to see Razumikhin
reading.explain: He suddenly recalls that he had set out for Vasilyevsky Island, to see Razumikhin.

reading.ru: Это был необыкновенно веселый и сообщительный парень, добрый до простоты.
reading.question: How is Razumikhin described as a person?
options: An unusually cheerful and sociable fellow, kind to the point of simplicity
A gloomy, withdrawn, and suspicious man
A cold and calculating businessman
A frail, sickly student
reading.correct: An unusually cheerful and sociable fellow, kind to the point of simplicity
reading.explain: The narrator describes Razumikhin as an unusually cheerful and sociable young man, kind to the point of artlessness.
